context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether the RBA can still deliver the hike that AONIA October has almost fully priced now that the mortgage/housing transmission channel is already contracting. If housing volumes, stamp-duty receipts and dwelling values keep falling, the Board's next decision cannot validate a 21.5bp October implied tightening from a 4.35 AONIA overnight without accepting a deeper activity/consumer break. The October contract is the first dated closer; a hold or a dovish skip should reprice implied AONIA toward overnight, and a delivered hike validates the market's assumption.

Inference: that is too much hike for a Board staring at falling turnover, a stamp-duty collapse and cooling activity/labor/consumer gauges, so the dated October decision is the mechanism that should reprice the contract lower if they hold. Unknown: whether inflation 82 is sufficient for them to hike through the housing evidence. Valuation without that meeting can stay wrong; the meeting is why this is a trade rather than a 99th-percentile AU 2Y fade.

holes_in_opposing_case: The booked direction contradicts the stated thesis. Packet futures are marked in implied-rate space. Short AONIA_2026-10 profits if implied AONIA rises (pay / AU rates up). Mean-reverter's structure and thesis say short implied / receive / fade remaining hikes (AU rates down). Those are opposite P&L signs on the same contract. The opposite-direction conflict is a sign error, not a second dated mechanism.

Taken literally as pay, the trade has no catalyst path and the wrong skew. October implied 4.565 versus overnight 4.35 already maps to about 21.5bp of a 25bp hike. Paying that residual wins only the leftover ~3.5bp if the RBA delivers and loses the 21.5bp if they hold. Housing evidence dated 16 Sep (stamp-duty -24% YoY, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne >7% off peak) is new transmission that attacks delivery, not a reason to buy more hike premium. Inflation gauge 82 is known, not new, and cannot by itself reprice a near-fully-priced hike higher.

Taken as the intended receive, the extra apparatus is not a closer. AU 2Y 4.999 sitting 13.9bp through Mar-27 AONIA 4.86 is a sovereign-versus-path residual, not a dated event. The 99th-percentile AU 2Y rank is explicitly a discovery flag in their own writeup, then reused as 'through the path' residual to justify a 1-3 month strip. Valuation without a meeting date can stay wrong. October IB is the event; Mar-27 AONIA (OI 201, volume 1) is not a mean-reversion instrument.
Carry_view supports_trade is false for a receive on an upward AONIA curve (Oct 4.565 vs overnight 4.35). A delayed-not-cancelled hike bleeds via roll. That is an event payoff, not positive carry.
'Crowded extrapolation' is asserted while CFTC/CME overlays are unavailable. Absence of positioning is not evidence of crowding and cannot support a fade-the-crowd overlay on IB.

attack: Strongest opposing claim: remaining Oct-Mar AONIA hike premium is stretched because housing is already binding and AU 2Y prints through the live path, so the extra 21-51bp should be faded over 1-3 months.

That claim does not support short AONIA_2026-10. If they want implied AONIA down, the paper book requires long the implied-rate mark, which is the original long. If they keep direction short, they are paying an 86%-priced October hike into fresh housing contraction — the opposite of their causal mechanism.

The 13.9bp AU 2Y-versus-Mar-27 AONIA gap can be read either way: 2Y rich to path, or path cheap to 2Y. Using it to justify both 'fade hikes in AONIA' and a short implied-rate booking is incoherent. A path-cheap reading would be a pay thesis; housing 16 Sep evidence rejects that reading for October.

Catalysts listed as 'housing/labor prints and RBA communication' are open-ended. Communication without a dated decision is not a closer. The October contract expires around the first meeting window; that is the mechanism. Extending into Nov/Mar without locking a separate markable strip on the conflicted instrument smuggles illiquid back-end duration into an event trade.

Inflation 82 is the real hawkish risk, already in the original invalidation. It is a reason to size down or to define the hold-versus-hike binary, not a reason to flip to pay or to wait 1-3 months for a percentile to mean-revert.
defense: Original stands: long AONIA_2026-10, receive, AU rates down, through the October RBA window. Packet mid remains implied 4.565 / price 95.435. Stop stays null. No new levels.

Fact versus inference versus unknown is unchanged. Fact: Oct implied 4.565 vs AONIA 4.35 after 16 Sep housing prints. Inference: the next meeting cannot deliver that near-full hike without ignoring a contracting housing channel and cooling activity/labor/consumer gauges (54/50/48). Unknown: exact meeting date inside the contract, and whether inflation 82 still dominates.

Expression remains rates-first. The mispricing is the October policy residual. Short AUDUSD is still the inferior alternative (76th percentile, Fed/SR3 contamination). Mean-reverter agrees AUDUSD is not stretched; that does not create an opposite rates view.

Would concede the argument if the RBA delivers the priced 25bp and ratifies 4.565, or if subsequent AU inflation keeps the gauge at 82 while housing volumes and stamp-duty stabilize. Mixed AU-US 2Y analog 3m outcomes (2025-07-30 reverse higher; 2026-04-23 continue cheaper) are not a concession: they are why the meeting, not the percentile, is the trade.

Uncertainty preserved: inflation 82 can still produce a hike-through-housing outcome; CFTC is missing; October timing inside the contract is not in the packet. None of that converts a receive event into a short implied-rate mean-reversion.
